title: Shortening door-to-needle time at a regional primary stroke centre through process mapping and PDSA cycles
abstract: Problem: median door-to-needle time of 62 minutes with 27 percent treated within 45 minutes. Intervention: mapping with all staff involved and four PDSA cycles (direct to CT, single group page, drug preparation during CT, out-of-hours extension) with nurse-led debriefs. Measures: door-to-needle time per case on a run chart; haemorrhage, treated mimics and trauma delays as balancing measures. Results will be written after June 2027.
introduction: Faster thrombolysis improves recovery after ischaemic stroke. Time studies place most delay between arrival and CT and between CT and the treatment decision, and small centres struggle to see change in monthly figures.
methods: The Model for Improvement guided two mapping sessions and four PDSA cycles from January to June 2027. Every case was plotted on a run chart with rules fixed before cycle 1, and the project was screened as quality improvement.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will show the run chart of every case with cycle dates marked, the step-time charts and the balancing measures with numerators and denominators.
discussion: The discussion will relate chart signals to the cycles and consider out-of-hours cases separately. It will review every treated mimic and haemorrhage against the speed gained.
limitations: This is a single centre with about 50 cases, and balancing measures are too rare to compare statistically. Secular changes in the regional network may contribute.
conclusion: To be written after the final cycle. It will report whether the aim was met and which changes the centre will keep.
